key_insight: GREx generalizes referring-expression tasks by supporting multi-target and no-target expressions, moving beyond the traditional one-expression–one-object assumption and providing a unified evaluation for segmentation, comprehension, and generation.
problem_solved: Existing datasets and methods assume single-target expressions only, which prevents models from handling real-world cases where expressions refer to multiple objects or to none at all; GREx addresses this gap with new data and evaluation protocols.
method: Introduce a generalized benchmark (three new datasets) that includes single-target, multi-target, and no-target expressions across segmentation, comprehension, and generation tasks.
Define unified task formulations and evaluation metrics that handle multi-target outputs and explicitly penalize/score no-target cases.
Provide baseline models and protocol for training/evaluation to enable consistent comparison across RES, REC, and REG in the generalized setting.
impact: Enables development and fair evaluation of vision–language models that work in realistic settings (ambiguous, multi-object, or absent referents), improving robustness and applicability of referring-expression systems in real-world applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side image examples showing (a) single-target, (b) multi-target, and (c) no-target referring expressions with corresponding segmentation masks/boxes and generated expressions.
Pipeline diagram illustrating unified RES/REC/REG flow: input image + expression → comprehension/segmentation/generation outputs with decision for no-target.
Bar chart comparing baseline performance across traditional vs. generalized benchmarks to show performance gaps and challenges.
Icon-based legend showing types of expressions (single, multi, none) and associated evaluation metrics for quick reference.
paper_title: GREx: Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation, Comprehension, and Generation
paper_authors: Henghui Ding, Chang Liu, Shuting He, Xudong Jiang, Yu-Gang Jiang
